title: TS SDK: negotiated stream handshake and checkpointed consumer examples
creator: Ethan Cole
description:
Problem: Customers are confused about best practices when interoperating between AsyncIterator-based consumers (Node/Deno) and browser Web Streams. Current SDK samples show one-off adapters; they lack a minimal negotiation/handshake that allows resumed reads after transient network errors and a stable 'checkpoint token' for retry semantics.

Goal: Ship a reference implementation + docs and examples that: 1) define a light-weight handshake chunk emitted at the start of a streamed response that carries a stable sequence offset and optional checkpoint token; 2) provide SDK-level utilities for converting AsyncIterator<Uint8Array | string> <-> ReadableStream (web) with checkpoint resume support; 3) document retry semantics and small example apps (Node worker, browser fetch + TransformStream) so customers can adopt patterns with minimal cognitive load.
acceptance_criteria:
- SDK exposes two helper constructors: makeNegotiatedReadableStream(adapterOptions) and makeCheckpointedAsyncIterable(stream, opts)
- Examples for browser and Node/Deno are included in the repo docs and CI examples folder
- Unit tests cover handshake parsing, checkpoint token propagation, and resume on simulated transient errors
- Integration test that replays a 3-chunk stream with a mid-stream disconnect and validates consumer resumes using checkpoint token
- Docs include clear guidance on when to rely on checkpoint resume vs full-retry (idempotency guidance)
proposal:
Introduce a minimal negotiation header protocol for streamed responses. The first logical chunk must be a JSON 'handshake' sentinel with these fields: {"offset": <number>, "checkpoint": <opaque string | null>, "mime": <string>}. This sentinel is not part of user payload and SDK adapters should filter it out before delivering items to user callbacks.

SDK surface:
- exports.makeNegotiatedReadableStream(responseBody, opts) -> ReadableStream
- exports.makeCheckpointedAsyncIterable(webStream, opts) -> AsyncIterable<string | Uint8Array>
- opts.retryPolicy: { maxAttempts, backoffMs, preserveOrder: boolean }
- opts.checkpointDeserializer/serializer optional hooks for app-specific tokens

Behavior: On network failure, the SDK will attempt retry according to retryPolicy. If a checkpoint token was seen from the handshake, SDK will re-issue a request with ?resume_token=<token> and will stream only missing chunks from that offset. If no token present, fallback to conservative full-retry semantics and emit a RecoverableError event to the consumer.
migration_notes:
Backwards compatibility: servers that do not emit a handshake will continue to work. makeNegotiatedReadableStream will treat the first non-JSON chunk as regular payload. However customers are encouraged to upgrade server-side response to include handshake for reliable resume. Migration doc includes a tiny server snippet (Node/Go) showing how to emit the handshake then the payload.

Versioning: feature gated behind ts-sdk-2.8.0. Consumers can opt-in; default not to try resume unless checkpoint token present in handshake.
test_plan:
- Unit tests: handshakeserializer/parse, filter-out-first-chunk, checkpoint token round-trip
- Simulated network: use msw/undici mock to drop connection after N bytes and assert resume occurs and consumer receives no duplicates
- Cross-runtime examples: run browser example in playwright that simulates navigator.onLine toggles; run Node example in CI using nock to simulate partial stream
- Fuzz: randomized offsets and checkpoint tokens to ensure parser is robust to mixed binary/text frames
- Performance: ensure adapters add <1% median latency on hot paths; measure allocations for typical 4KB chunks
rollout_plan:
1) Implement feature behind flag in canary branch; add unit/integration tests.
2) Ship to SDK canary (ts-sdk-canary) and publish examples under /examples/stream-handshake.
3) Ask early-access customers (two existing customers using streaming) to try canary.
4) Monitor errors and duplicate-chunk telemetry for 72 hours.
5) Flip default opt-in for ts-sdk-2.8.0 if stable.

Telemetry: add metrics for handshake_seen, resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, duplicate_chunk_count.
risks_mitigation:
- Risk: servers may emit handshake incompatible shapes. Mitigation: keep handshake parsing permissive; ignore unknown fields. Provide server snippet and tests.
- Risk: duplicate delivery on partial retries. Mitigation: rely on offset semantics in handshake and only de-duplicate based on numeric offset + chunk boundaries. Add strict tests.
- Risk: customers rely on SDK opaque behavior. Mitigation: document exact semantics and provide opt-out flag.
- Risk: added API surface increases maintenance. Mitigation: implement small, well-documented helpers with minimal dependencies.
